newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan gasoline station lets you primp as you pump.
newsitem.headline: Japan gasoline station lets you primp as you pump.

text.p: Looking for a hot oil treatment?
In Japan, you can now get one for your car and your hair, simultaneously.

In a mad scramble to add body to rapidly receding profit margins, Japan's gasoline stations are trying just about everything these days -- all the way from noodle shops to drive-though laundry service.
Now, from Japan Energy Corp comes the "Hair Station", where auto service coupled with a second-floor beauty salon make a bouffant and a battery charge a one-stop shop.

In addition to the regular pumping crew, a staff of two hairstylists has been hired to provide haircuts priced at around 2,500 yen ($21) for a basic cut -- a relative bargain in Tokyo, where a visit to the hair salon typically sets customers back by between $50 and $100.
The average turn-around time per cut is 15 minutes, a Japan Energy spokesman said.
Colourings, permanents and the full line of salon treatments are also available, the spokesman said.
The first site, located in Mitaka on the western outskirts of Tokyo, will serve as a six-month experiment which will determine the future of hair station outlets.
"We will make an assessment based on performance in the first six months, before we open additional sites," the company said on Monday.

Japan's gasoline stations, battered by a two-year price war and industry rationalisation which will see their numbers cut by more than one-third over the next five years, face increasing pressure to diversify their businesses in order to survive.

Analysts say profit margins at the pump have withered to nothing for many stations since government deregulation beginning in 1996 broke the companies' oil product import monopoly and caused a free-fall in retail gasoline prices.
Average pump prices in Japan hit a decade-low 102 yen per litre in July, and they are falling still.

The steady downward trend was enough to make Cosmo Oil Co Ltd rip out the pumps from one of its service stations in Yokohama last November and launched a drive-through laundry business -- complete with a field staff which allows customers to remain in the comfort of their cars while picking up or dropping off clothing.
Cosmo says revenues at the site have more than doubled since the switch.

Cosmo, also experimenting with joint gasoline station-noodle shops, plans a second "strictly cleaning" site by the end of the summer, and, by the end of this year, sites where drivers can simultaneously receive their laundry and have their tanks filled with petrol.

British Petroleum Co Plc, which fierce competition in Europe has made an old hand at pumping station hybrids, plans to enter Japan's gasoline market by the end of this year -- with a campaign to build as many as 100 stations as annexes to major supermarket chain Iseya Kosan over the next few years. ($1=116 yen)
